               {diagnose,generate,maintain,recommend,install-skills,find,fleet,lint,portability,eval,decision}

positional arguments:
  {diagnose,generate,maintain,recommend,install-skills,find,fleet,lint,portability,eval,decision}
    diagnose            Diagnose the AI agent setup of one or more projects. :param project_roots:
                        one or more paths to project directories :param format: output format —
                        'text' or 'json' :param verbose: show additional detail in text output
                        :param min_score: minimum overall score to pass (exit 0); below this exits
                        1
    generate            Generate missing AI setup artifacts for one or more projects. By default,
                        shows what would be created (dry run). Use --write to actually write
                        files. Existing files are never overwritten. :param project_roots: one or
                        more paths to project directories :param write: actually write files
                        (default: dry run) :param format: output format — 'text' or 'json' :param
                        agents_md: also generate AGENTS.md (cross-platform agent instructions)
                        :param hooks: also generate starter hook scripts
    maintain            Check for stale references, out-of-sync docs, and other drift. Each
                        finding carries a recommended triage: align (update the config to match
                        the code), revert (restore the code the config describes) or ignore (a
                        legitimately volatile reference: put `opsward: ignore-path` on its line).
                        :param project_roots: one or more paths to project directories :param
                        format: output format — 'text' or 'json'
    recommend           Recommend ecosystem skills based on the project's tech stack. Analyzes
                        dependencies and suggests skills from the community catalog. :param
                        project_roots: one or more paths to project directories :param format:
                        output format — 'text' or 'json'
    install-skills      Install opsward's Claude Code skills (and agents) into a project or
                        globally. By default, shows what would be created (dry run). Use --write
                        to actually write files. Existing files are never overwritten. :param
                        target: project directory (ignored when --global is set) :param
                        global_install: install into ~/.claude/ instead of the project :param
                        agents: also install agent definitions (default: True) :param write:
                        actually write files (default: dry run)
    find                Find assets (skills, agents, docs) across one or more projects by QUERY.
                        Cross-repo asset discovery via the toolery package (install with: pip
                        install 'opsward[discovery]'). :param query: search query :param
                        project_roots: one or more project directories (default: current dir)
                        :param kinds: comma-separated asset kinds — skill, agent, doc :param
                        semantic: use toolery's ir semantic backend (needs toolery[ir]) :param
                        limit: max results to show
    fleet               Diagnose many projects at once and roll the results up into one fleet
                        report. The fleet is the given roots, plus the git repos found under
                        --under. With --manifest the fleet is remembered: the roots and the latest
                        summary are written to that JSON file, and a later run with only
                        --manifest re-diagnoses the same roots (given roots or --under replace
                        them). The manifest holds this machine's absolute paths, so keep it out of
                        version control. Exits 1 when any root could not be diagnosed. :param
                        project_roots: project directories to diagnose :param under: also diagnose
                        every git repo found under this directory :param depth: how many levels
                        below --under to look for git repos :param format: output format — 'text'
                        or 'json' (the name-keyed summary) :param manifest: JSON file that
                        remembers the fleet's roots and its latest summary
    lint                Check skill specs and the hooks config: pass or fail, no score (exit 1 on
                        any finding). The strict counterpart of `diagnose --min-score`, for CI and
                        pre-commit. Validators: opsward (its own agentskills.io check, always
                        there), skill (the skill package's validate(); pip install
                        'opsward[lint]'), and the external agnix and skillcheck linters (opt-in by
                        name). auto runs opsward and skill, each when installed. :param
                        project_roots: one or more project directories (default: current dir)
                        :param validators: 'auto', or a comma list of: opsward, skill, agnix,
                        skillcheck :param format: output format — 'text' or 'json'
    portability         Show which agent hosts find project instructions, and how renders drift
                        from AGENTS.md. One row per host (claude, codex, copilot, cursor, ...)
                        with how it is covered: symlink, import (an @AGENTS.md shim), native
                        (reads AGENTS.md itself), copy, rules, or none. Then every section where a
                        render differs from AGENTS.md. Report-only. :param project_roots: one or
                        more project directories (default: current dir) :param format: output
                        format — 'text' or 'json'
    eval                Report-only evals of a project's agent setup: an LLM judge of CLAUDE.md,
                        and golden tasks. The judge scores CLAUDE.md's subjective dimensions next
                        to the rubric's own score. The golden tasks (a JSON list of {name, prompt,
                        expect, forbid}, by default <docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json) run with and
                        without CLAUDE.md and report the pass-rate delta. --judge rubric is free
                        and deterministic (the rubric judge and an agent that quotes the config:
                        it checks the harness, not a model); --judge anthropic makes paid calls
                        (pip install 'opsward[eval]'). Exits 0 whenever it ran (a report, never a
                        gate); 2 only on a usage error. :param project_root: the project directory
                        :param judge: 'rubric' (free) or 'anthropic' (paid model calls) :param
                        samples: judge samples per dimension (the median is reported) :param
                        tasks: golden-tasks JSON file (default: <docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json, if
                        present) :param runs: runs per golden task and arm :param format: output
                        format — 'text' or 'json'
    decision

usage: opsward fleet [-h] [-u UNDER] [-d DEPTH] [-f FORMAT] [-m MANIFEST] [project-roots ...]

Diagnose many projects at once and roll the results up into one fleet report.

The fleet is the given roots, plus the git repos found under --under. With --manifest
the fleet is remembered: the roots and the latest summary are written to that JSON
file, and a later run with only --manifest re-diagnoses the same roots (given roots or
--under replace them). The manifest holds this machine's absolute paths, so keep it
out of version control. Exits 1 when any root could not be diagnosed.

:param project_roots: project directories to diagnose
:param under: also diagnose every git repo found under this directory
:param depth: how many levels below --under to look for git repos
:param format: output format — 'text' or 'json' (the name-keyed summary)
:param manifest: JSON file that remembers the fleet's roots and its latest summary

  project-roots         -

                        ''

usage: opsward eval [-h] [-j JUDGE] [-s SAMPLES] [-t TASKS] [-r RUNS] [-f FORMAT] project-root

Report-only evals of a project's agent setup: an LLM judge of CLAUDE.md, and golden tasks.

The judge scores CLAUDE.md's subjective dimensions next to the rubric's own score. The
golden tasks (a JSON list of {name, prompt, expect, forbid}, by default
<docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json) run with and without CLAUDE.md and report the pass-rate
delta. --judge rubric is free and deterministic (the rubric judge and an agent that
quotes the config: it checks the harness, not a model); --judge anthropic makes paid
calls (pip install 'opsward[eval]'). Exits 0 whenever it ran (a report, never a gate);
2 only on a usage error.

:param project_root: the project directory
:param judge: 'rubric' (free) or 'anthropic' (paid model calls)
:param samples: judge samples per dimension (the median is reported)
:param tasks: golden-tasks JSON file (default: <docs>/evals/golden_tasks.json, if present)
:param runs: runs per golden task and arm
:param format: output format — 'text' or 'json'

positional arguments:
  project-root          -

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -j JUDGE, --judge JUDGE
                        'rubric'
  -s SAMPLES, --samples SAMPLES
                        1
  -t TASKS, --tasks TASKS
                        ''
  -r RUNS, --runs RUNS  1
  -f FORMAT, --format FORMAT
                        'text'
